questions.ground_truth: The Secretary has an opportunity to approve planning or design documents prepared by a Self-Governance Tribe only if there is an amendment to the construction project agreement that results in a significant change in the original scope of work.

questions.question: What is the deadline for a manufacturer to submit a rebate reduction request due to a severe supply chain disruption caused by a natural disaster or other unexpected event?
questions.ground_truth: The manufacturer must submit the rebate reduction request within 60 calendar days from the first day that the natural disaster or other unique or unexpected event occurred or began. This timeline applies to events occurring on or after August 2, 2024.

questions.question: Starting when are PDP sponsors and MA organizations required to offer the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan option to their enrollees?
questions.ground_truth: PDP sponsors and MA organizations must provide the Medicare Prescription Payment Plan option for plan years beginning on or after January 1, 2026, or for non-calendar year plans, for the portion of the plan year starting on January 1, 2026.

questions.question: What documentation and data submission requirements must a Medicare Diabetes Prevention Program supplier fulfill regarding beneficiary identification and performance data?
questions.ground_truth: An MDPP supplier must submit a crosswalk file containing Medicare Beneficiary Identifiers for each MDPP beneficiary receiving services to CMS or its contractor. Additionally, the supplier must submit performance data for beneficiaries who attended ongoing maintenance sessions using data elements consistent with the CDC's DPRP standards for the core services period.

questions.question: Under 42 CFR § 423.104, what is the maximum number of specialty tiers that a Part D plan may maintain?
questions.ground_truth: A Part D plan may maintain up to two specialty tiers, as specified in section (d)(2)(iv)(D).

questions.question: Under 42 CFR § 71.50, what activities are included within the definition of use for scientific research?
questions.ground_truth: Use for scientific research includes research projects following a defined protocol and standards as normally conducted at the university level, as well as safety testing, potency testing, and other activities related to the production of medical products.

questions.question: What types of entities are eligible to receive grants authorized by section 445 of the Act for Alzheimer's disease research?
questions.ground_truth: Public or private nonprofit entities, including university medical centers, are eligible to receive grants authorized by section 445 of the Act. These entities must conduct basic and clinical research (including multidisciplinary research) into, training in, and demonstration of advanced diagnostic, prevention, and treatment methods for Alzheimer's disease.

questions.question: What radiation weighting factors does NIOSH use when calculating equivalent doses for dose reconstruction?
questions.ground_truth: NIOSH uses the current, standard radiation weighting factors from the International Commission on Radiological Protection when calculating equivalent doses for the occupational exposure matrix.

questions.question: What information about incidents and shipments must an applicant provide when renewing a special permit for hazardous materials transportation?
questions.ground_truth: The applicant must provide a statement regarding all operational, shipping, and incident experience of which they are aware since the special permit's issuance or most recent renewal. The statement must indicate the approximate number of shipments made or packages shipped, and the number of shipments or packages involved in any loss of contents, including loss by venting other than as authorized. If the applicant is aware of no incidents, they must certify this fact.

questions.question: What four criteria must an activity meet to be classified as a covered task under 49 CFR § 195.501?
questions.ground_truth: According to 49 CFR § 195.501(b), a covered task must: (1) be performed on a pipeline facility; (2) be an operations or maintenance task; (3) be performed as a requirement of this part; and (4) affect the operation or integrity of the pipeline. The operator identifies which activities meet these criteria.

questions.question: What steps should be taken to establish an independent voting trust to avoid control violations?
questions.ground_truth: According to 49 CFR § 1013.1(a), the independent voting trust should be established before a controlling block of voting securities is purchased in order to avoid an unlawful control violation.

questions.question: Does unequal aggregate expenditure between male and female athletic teams automatically constitute noncompliance under 49 CFR § 25.450?
questions.ground_truth: No. Unequal aggregate expenditures for members of each sex or unequal expenditures for male and female teams will not automatically constitute noncompliance. However, the designated agency official may consider the failure to provide necessary funds for teams for one sex when assessing equality of opportunity for members of each sex.

questions.question: What is the requalification period for DOT-3AL cylinders made of aluminum alloy 6351-T6 that undergo eddy current examination combined with visual inspection for sustained load cracking?
questions.ground_truth: The requalification period is 5 years. Cylinders must undergo eddy current examination in accordance with Appendix C and visual inspection in accordance with CGA Pamphlet C-6.1, with condemnation required if any crack in the neck or shoulder is 2 thread lengths or more.

questions.question: What must a railroad do after its inspection, testing, and maintenance program is approved by the FRA?
questions.ground_truth: After FRA approval, the railroad must adopt and comply with the program, and perform all inspections, tests, maintenance tasks, and procedures described in the program in accordance with the procedures, criteria, and intervals that the railroad identified as safety-critical.

questions.question: What ambient temperature range must be maintained when conducting the overcharge test for electric vehicle REESS safety controls?
questions.ground_truth: The overcharge test must be conducted at ambient temperatures between 10 °C and 30 °C, as specified in section S12.1 of the standard.

questions.question: When both parties voluntarily consent to mediation, does the Board hold the underlying proceeding in abeyance and toll statutory deadlines?
questions.ground_truth: Yes. When both parties voluntarily consent to mediation, the Board may direct that a proceeding be held in abeyance pending the conclusion of mediation, and the period during which any proceeding is held in abeyance shall toll applicable statutory deadlines.

questions.question: For vehicles manufactured between September 1, 2001 and September 1, 2002, what percentage of vehicles must comply with S7 requirements under Standard No. 201?
questions.ground_truth: At least 70 percent of vehicles manufactured during this period must comply with S7 requirements. This compliance percentage is calculated based on either the manufacturer's average annual production from September 1, 1999 to September 1, 2002, or the manufacturer's production during the September 1, 2001 to September 1, 2002 period, whichever is applicable.

questions.question: Can a manufacturer use test data from a complete sister vehicle instead of performing tests on a cab-complete vehicle for fuel consumption certification?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, manufacturers may submit test data from the complete sister vehicle instead of performing the test on the cab-complete vehicle for fuel consumption certification purposes, provided the cab-complete vehicles are tested using the same equivalent test weight and other dynamometer settings that apply for the complete sister vehicle.

questions.question: Can a transit agency designate key staff or committees to support the SMS Executive and other safety personnel in developing and implementing the SMS?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, according to 49 CFR § 673.23(5), a transit agency may designate key staff, groups of staff, or committees to support the Accountable Executive, Chief Safety Officer, Safety Committee, or SMS Executive in developing, implementing, and operating the transit agency's SMS.

questions.question: According to 49 CFR § 393.5, what is the definition of an emergency brake system and what does it NOT include as a failure?
questions.ground_truth: An emergency brake system is a mechanism designed to stop a vehicle after a single failure occurs in the service brake system of a part designed to contain compressed air or brake fluid or vacuum. However, it does not include failure of a common valve, manifold brake fluid housing, or brake chamber housing.

questions.question: What old classification system is referenced in this regulation for comparing hazard classes, and what is the cutoff date for when this old system was in effect?
questions.ground_truth: The regulation references the classification system that was in effect prior to January 1, 1991. This old system used classifications such as Class A, Class B, and Class C explosives, along with blasting agents, which are compared to the current Division 1.1 through 1.6 classifications in the provided table.

questions.question: When evaluating a person's prior safety conduct with a different railroad, what is the earliest date that a railroad may consider information about that person's prior safety conduct?
questions.ground_truth: According to 49 CFR § 246.113(g)(1), a railroad shall not consider information concerning prior safety conduct that occurred prior to July 22, 2024. Therefore, July 22, 2024 is the earliest date that prior safety conduct information may be considered.

questions.question: Does a passenger vessel that is rented or leased to and operated solely by consumers fall under the definition of 'passenger vessel' in 49 CFR § 39.3?
questions.ground_truth: No. According to 49 CFR § 39.3, the definition of 'passenger vessel' explicitly excludes boats or other craft rented or leased to and operated solely by consumers.

questions.question: Under 49 CFR § 177.835, can a motor vehicle transporting Class 1 explosive materials also carry metal articles in the same load, and if so, what conditions must be met?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, a motor vehicle transporting Class 1 explosive materials may transport metal or other articles likely to damage explosives, but only if the different parts of the load are segregated or secured in place and separated by bulkheads or other suitable means to prevent damage to the explosive materials or their packages.

questions.question: Under 49 CFR § 176.3, what are the conditions under which a carrier is prohibited from transporting hazardous materials by vessel?
questions.ground_truth: A carrier may not transport by vessel any hazardous material that is not prepared for transportation in accordance with parts 172 and 173, or as authorized by subpart C of part 171. Additionally, a carrier may not transport by vessel any explosive or explosive composition described in § 173.54.

questions.question: How is Target RB1 located on a roll-bar according to Standard No. 201?
questions.ground_truth: Target RB1 is located on the roll-bar within a longitudinal vertical plane (Plane 30) positioned at the mid-sagittal plane of a dummy seated in any outboard designated seating position. The target is positioned at the location on the roll-bar that is closest to either CG-F2 or CG-R, as appropriate for the same dummy.

questions.question: What is the maximum capacity for an inner packaging containing a hazardous liquid material permitted under 49 CFR § 173.13(c)(1)(i)?
questions.ground_truth: The maximum capacity for an inner packaging is 1.2 L. However, the net quantity of liquid in any inner packaging may not exceed 1 L when measured at 20°C (68°F). Additionally, sufficient outage must be provided to ensure the inner packaging will not become liquid full at 55°C (130°F).

questions.question: When testing a child restraint system on an aircraft passenger seat, what must the manufacturer do if no instructions are provided for orienting the restraint when the seat back angle is adjusted?
questions.ground_truth: If the manufacturer recommendations do not include instructions for orienting the restraint in aircraft when the restraint seat back angle is adjusted to any position, the manufacturer must position the restraint on the aircraft seat by following the instructions provided for orienting the restraint in motor vehicles.

questions.question: Can a motor carrier transport Division 2.3 poisonous gas materials in the same motor vehicle with foodstuffs if the poisonous material is overpacked in a metal drum?
questions.ground_truth: Yes, a motor carrier may transport Division 2.3 poisonous gas or Division 6.1 poisonous materials in the same motor vehicle with foodstuffs, feed, or edible material if the poisonous material is packaged in accordance with the subchapter and is either overpacked in a metal drum as specified in § 173.25(c) or loaded into a closed unit load device with the foodstuffs loaded into another closed unit load device.

questions.question: What types of entities are eligible to apply to the Chief Counsel for a determination regarding whether a state or local requirement is preempted under 49 CFR § 107.202?
questions.ground_truth: Any person directly affected by a requirement of a state, political subdivision, or Indian tribe may apply, including the state or political subdivision itself or an Indian tribe. However, this does not apply to highway routing matters covered under 49 U.S.C. 5125(c).

questions.question: During what hours must records be made available for inspection and copying by FRA representatives under 49 CFR § 214.533?
questions.ground_truth: Records must be available for inspection and copying during normal business hours by representatives of FRA and States participating under part 212 of this chapter.

questions.question: What are the font size and language requirements for the statement that must be provided to the first purchaser of a motor vehicle manufactured on or after September 1, 1990?
questions.ground_truth: The statement must be provided in writing in the English language and not less than 10 point type. It must be included in the owner's manual or, if there is no owner's manual, on a one-page document.

questions.question: What are the six categories of roadway work mentioned in 49 CFR § 671.39 for which redundant protections must be identified?
questions.ground_truth: The six categories include: (1) roadway workers moving from one track zone location to another; (2) roadway workers performing minor tasks; (3) roadway workers conducting visual inspections; (4) roadway workers using hand tools, machines, or equipment in conducting testing of track system components or non-visual inspections; (5) roadway workers using hand tools, machines, or equipment in performing maintenance, construction, or repairs; and (6) lone workers accessing the roadway or track zone or performing visual inspections or minor tasks.
